shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Cross-level combat, senses, NPC travel, CE bridge (experimental), "Traveler" climb animations, blueprint art, wall risers, research-gated links, a per-colony off switch, Perspective Shift + Toggleable Overlays support. Window 13 inverts click-through to a GLOBAL opt-out at UI.MouseCell/MouseMapPosition (dev tools, psycasts, jumps, mortars and foreign mods all see through air for free) and fixes PS's "return to character" - both field-verified. CE manned-turret compat is open.

**⚠ THE ONE THING NO WINDOW HAS EVER DONE: THE WORKSHOP SMOKE TEST.** Every verification, all fifteen windows, has been against the WORKSPACE copy; nobody has ever subscribed to the uploaded item and loaded it. **⚠ USER WORKING RULES:** (1) NEVER source design ideas from other mods unless asked - scans COMPAT ONLY. **V1 is OUR OWN prior work and is exempt.** (2) Building art = USER via Nano Banana kits. (3) About.xml description = USER's copy. (4) N mockups = N CHOICES.

**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity.

**⚠⚠ THE SEVENTY-ONE RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. COUNT EMITTERS/POPULATIONS/ENGINE STACKS. 5 (§48): A `Touch` TARGET IS USUALLY UNWALKABLE. 6 (§49): A VANILLA HELPER CAN BE A NO-OP INSTEAD OF AN ERROR. 7 (§52): THE CARVE IS NOT THE LAST WORD. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS NOT A CELL. 11 (§55): A CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): **NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE** - grep version at rule 54. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE - selectable is drawable, and so is **highlightable** (§83). 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW - and §84.8's other half: when a thing insists on drawing itself at a position of its OWN, the offset must be applied to THAT position. 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL. 43 (§78): **DEFER THE MOVE, NEVER THE DECISION.** 44 (§78b): AN OFFSET APPLIED WHOLE ON FRAME ONE IS A TELEPORT. 45 (§78d): **A DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOT A DIRECTION OF ELEVATION.** 46 (§78d): **NON-UNIFORM SCALE x ROTATION = SHEAR.** 47 (§79): **A FOREIGN MOD'S CACHED CURSOR CELL IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT COORDINATE SPACE.** 48 (§81a): **A WRITE THAT IS READ BACK BY ITS OWN CALLER IS NOT A WRITE.** 49 (§0c): **A TEST THAT PROVES FEATURE A SAYS NOTHING ABOUT FEATURE B.** 50 (§82a): **TWO OF OUR OWN PATCHES ON ONE VANILLA METHOD CANCEL SILENTLY.** GREP OUR OWN `[HarmonyPatch]` LIST FIRST. 51 (§82b): **A FACTORY HAS USUALLY CONSUMED ITS INPUT BY THE TIME THE POSTFIX RUNS.** 52 (§83a): **AN OVERLAY MUST ASK THE SAME QUESTION THE CLICK WILL ASK, AND IT MUST NOT BE A QUESTION THAT WRITES.** 53 (§83c): **A PREDICATE PASSED IN IS CLOSED OVER THE ARGUMENTS THE CALLER ALREADY HAS.** 54 (§84a): **A CLEAN GREP IS NOT AN ABSENCE - SEARCH FOR THE CAPABILITY, NOT THE TYPE NAME.** 55 (§84.3): **"AFTER THE DUTY HAD ITS TURN" INCLUDES A FALLBACK JOB YOU WOULD NEVER CALL A REAL ONE.** 56 (§84.5): **WHEN YOU RANK CANDIDATES BY ONE COST AND FILTER THEM BY ANOTHER, THE RANKING FINDS THE FILTER'S BLIND SPOT.** 57 (§85a): **WHEN TWO SUBSYSTEMS EACH ANSWER "WHICH SIDE OF THIS THING", ONE OF THEM IS ABOUT TO BE WRONG.** 58 (§85b): **A PROPERTY OF THE ART CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THE DEF.** 59 (§85.8): **`size` MUST BE MEASURED FROM THE DRAWING, NOT COPIED FROM `drawSize`.** 60 (§85.9): **MEASURE THE PIXELS; A DRAW OFFSET AND AN ART-OFFSET TABLE ARE THE SAME NUMBER TWICE.** 61 (§85c): **A COLOURED VERSION OF A GRAPHIC IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT, AND VANILLA HARD-CODES ITS TYPE.** 62 (§85d): **A TABLE OF FINISHED ANSWERS ROTS; STORE ONLY WHAT NOTHING ELSE OWNS AND DERIVE THE REST.** 63 (§85.14): **MEASURE A PATIENCE FROM THE EVENT IT NAMES.** 64 (§85.16): **A DIAGNOSTIC THAT IS OFF BY DEFAULT IS A DIAGNOSTIC THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** 65 (§85.17): **WHEN A DERIVED RULE IS RIGHT THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR, THE FOURTH IS A DEFECTIVE INPUT.** 66 (§85.19): **A DESTINATION CELL DOES NOT CONSTRAIN THE SIDE IT IS ENTERED FROM.** 67 (§85.20): **AN EARLY RETURN THAT PRESERVES STATE MUST ASK WHO SENT THE NEW ORDER.** 68 (§85.22): **WHEN THE SAME 'EXCEPTION' IS REPORTED TWICE ON ONE DEF, IT IS THE DEF'S RULE, NOT TWO EXCEPTIONS.** 69 (§86a): **WHEN YOU SUSPEND A FOREIGN MOD'S DRIVER, YOU INHERIT EVERY REQUEST THAT DRIVER SERVED.** A UI control can be nothing but a cleared field whose only consumer is the loop you switched off - it still draws, still responds, and does nothing. Enumerate what READS the state you neutralised, not just what writes it. 70 (§87a): **AN OPT-IN CORRECTION APPLIED AT N CONSUMERS IS A DEFAULT APPLIED AT THE WRONG LAYER.** Correct it at the source and enumerate the EXCEPTIONS - that list is finite, auditable and self-reporting, whereas the consumer list grows silently every time anyone adds a feature or installs a mod. 71 (§89): **A PROBE THAT ASKS FOR "THE" OCCUPANT CANNOT SEE A STACK.** `GetFirstPawn` + "is it me?" reports `none` for the one arrangement that matters - two pawns on one cell - so five runs of evidence said "nothing is in the way" while the pawn was standing in the way of itself. When a diagnostic exonerates a cell, check whether it COUNTED or merely peeked.

# 86. PERSPECTIVE SHIFT "RETURN TO CHARACTER" — **FIELD-VERIFIED #395**

`Source/Compat/PerspectiveShiftCompat.cs` only.

**⚠⚠ 86a THE BUTTON IS NOTHING BUT A CLEARED FIELD (rule 69).** Repro: avatar on the lower floor, double-click an upper-floor colonist on the colonist bar, press "Return to character" - nothing happened. PS's `Avatar_UI.DrawCameraLockReturnButton` draws only while `State.CameraLockPosition.HasValue`, and its entire click handler is `State.CameraLockPosition = null`. That works in vanilla PS because `Avatar.UpdateCamera` re-centres next frame. **§76 prefixes `UpdateCamera` out for the whole time the viewed band is not the avatar's** (rule 24), so the press cleared the field, the button vanished, and the camera never moved.

**86.2 WATCH THE FALLING EDGE, NOT `lockedByUs`.** `lockSeen` records the field's state each `SyncPeek`; a `true -> false` transition while `suspendCamera` is armed means "put me back on the avatar". ⚠ **In the reported repro the lock was set by PS ITSELF** - its `JumpToCurrentMapLoc` postfix fires on the colonist-bar jump - so `lockedByUs` is FALSE and an ownership test misses exactly the reported case. Every other PS path that nulls the field (a jump whose target IS the avatar's cell, `SetAvatar`, `ClearAvatar`, load) means the same thing and wants the same response.

**86.3 ORDER: BAND FIRST, RELEASE SECOND.** `ReturnToAvatar` calls `ABBandView.SetBand(avatar's band, preserveXZ:false)` and releases the suspend only once it SUCCEEDED - releasing first lets PS drag the camera toward a band our clip refuses to draw (the window-7 curtain bug). An undug band makes `SetBand` refuse with its own message and the peek is left intact, not half-torn-down. Then `SnapToAvatar` closes the distance so PS's 10%-a-frame lerp is a no-op.

**⚠ 86.4 RE-ENTRANCY IS REAL:** `SetBand` calls `SyncPeek` directly. `returning` guards it. `Release()` also clears `lockSeen` so a stale edge cannot survive a map change or a load.

# 87. GLOBAL CLICK-THROUGH — THE MODEL IS NOW OPT-OUT — **FIELD-VERIFIED #395**

`Source/V2/ABMouseDescend.cs` (new), edits to `ABCombatTargeting.cs` and `ABBelowClickThrough.cs`.

**⚠⚠ 87a THE INVERSION (rule 70).** User: "make all air tiles click-through by default to save on patches. Dev targeting, psycast targeting, jumping, combat, mortars all intuitively click through air tiles as they are not selectable anyhow." Since window 7 the descend was OPT-IN at four consumers, so every NEW consumer - a dev tool, another mod's targeter - started out broken and had to be noticed and patched. **The justification for inverting: there is no reading of "I clicked the empty sky" that means the sky.** Open air is Impassable, unselectable, unbuildable and undesignatable, so the raw answer is never the useful one.

**87.2 THE CHOKEPOINT IS TWO METHODS.** `UI.MouseCell` and `UI.MouseMapPosition`, both one-line wrappers over `UI.UIToMapPosition`. **⚠ THAT THIRD METHOD IS NOT PATCHED AND MUST NOT BE** - a pure screen-to-map transform also used for drag-box corners, the camera's own centre and map-to-UI round trips. Both wrappers are needed: vanilla resolves THINGS from a Vector3 clickPos but the bare CELL from `UI.MouseCell()`, and patching one is §82a.

**87.3 TWO FIELD-VERIFIED PATCHES DELETED AND TOMBSTONED.** `Patch_GenUI_ABThingsUnderMouseSeeThrough` and `Patch_GenUI_ABTargetsAtSeeThrough` (§82, #375) are redundant - vanilla finds below-level things natively now. **⚠ DO NOT REINSTATE EITHER**: alongside the global descend they are §82a a third time (`TryResolveClicked` asks "is this open air?" about a cell already resolved to floor, answers no, goes silently inert, and reads like the rule is firing when it is not).

**⚠⚠ 87.4 POINTING IS NOT ORDERING, AND KEEPING THEM APART IS WHAT MADE THIS SAFE.** "Which cell is under the cursor" is now global. "Where should these pawns go" also depends on the pawns and stays in `TryTranslateForOrder` - field-verified (§33b/§33f) and built entirely on a RAW cursor. Rather than rewrite it against a new input contract, **`Selector.HandleMapClicks` is SUPPRESSED** so it receives the value it always has. Same for left-click selection, whose curtain clamp compares the cursor against the VIEWED band's rows and **would have rejected every open-air click outright**. Verified in #395: right-click ordering unchanged.

**87.5 THE EXCLUSION LIST, THREE REASONS.** One `[HarmonyPatch]` + `TargetMethods` + a Finalizer, so the policy is auditable in one place.
- **(a) DESIGNATION AND PLACEMENT** - user's call: build and mine stay clamped (rule 1). `DesignatorManager.ProcessInputEvents/DesignatorManagerUpdate/DesignationManagerOnGUI`, `DesignationDragger.StartDrag/GetCurrentBoundary`, `Designator_Place.SelectedUpdate/DrawMouseAttachments/HandleRotation`. ⚠ The dragger is the sharp one: **a drag rect straddling a band seam designates across the gutter** - §46 in a new door. Both verified #395.
- **(b) A DELTA OF TWO MOUSE READS** - `CameraDriver.RootSize` setter. Zoom-to-mouse is `v = MouseMapPosition(); <zoom>; rootPos += v - MouseMapPosition()`, second read taken AFTER the camera moved; one read over air and one over floor gains a spurious Slot and **the camera jumps a level on a scroll notch** (rule 24). Verified #395.
- **(c) OURS ALREADY** - `Selector.HandleMapClicks` (also protects `dragBox.start`, which `DragBox.ScreenRect` projects back to screen), `Selector.SelectUnderMouse`, `Selector.SelectAllMatchingObjectUnderMouseOnScreen`, `MultiPawnGotoController.ProcessInputEvents` (preserves §33f; ledger 14).

**⚠ 87.5b THE LIST INCRIMINATES ITSELF (rule 33).** `TargetMethods` NAMES every entry it could not resolve and errors if it resolved NONE. A silently dropped null is one exclusion quietly removed; losing the CameraDriver entry alone presents as a camera bug with nothing tying it to a rename.

**⚠ 87.5c EXPLICIT RAW BEATS AMBIENT SUPPRESSION.** `Patch_Selector_ABSelectThrough` calls `ABMouseDescend.RawMouseMapPosition()` rather than trusting it runs inside a suppressed region - `Selector.SelectUnderMouse` has a third caller OUTSIDE `HandleMapClicks`, and that is exactly the kind of call-graph detail nobody re-checks.

**87.5d MECHANICS.** Memoised on `(frameCount, RAW cell)` - not frameCount alone, because OnGUI runs once per GUI EVENT and a MouseDown carries its own mouse position. The suppression counter is frame-stamped so a leak costs one frame instead of wedging pointing for the session. Gated on `ABGuard.Rendering` + `ABBelowClickThrough.Enabled` + `ABMouseDescend.Enabled`. `ABCombatTargeting.CounterReport` now reports the global descend.

**87.6 THE PASSING CHECKLIST (#395), reusable verbatim:** build ghost stays on the viewed level over air and refuses; drag-mine does not cross the seam; scroll-zoom over air does not jump a level; dev-spawn lands on the level seen through the hole; psycast/jump/mortar force-target through a hole; right-click orders unchanged same- and cross-level; left-click select through a hole; PS "return to character".

**87.7 RESIDUE.** Our own three probe call sites (`CelestialLightingCompat` x2, `ABBandWeather`) now read the DESCENDED cell - harmless for readouts, but CelestialLighting's probe prints "IDENTITY" where it used to print "SEE-THROUGH". Double-click select-all sits inside the suppressed `HandleMapClicks` and does not see through; it did not before either.

# 88. COMBAT EXTENDED — MANNED WEAPONS ("STATIONARY MACHINE GUNS") — **OPEN, NOT STARTED**

User picked the MANNED case specifically, not CE turrets in general.

**88.1 WHAT ALREADY WORKS.** The four §44 seams key on `Verb_LaunchProjectileCE`, `ShiftVecReport`, `ShiftTarget` and `ProjectileCE.Launch`, all of which a manned CE gun uses - shot legality, aim space, projectile origin and the high-ground suppression model are already band-aware for it.

**⚠⚠ 88a WHAT DOES NOT, FROM DECOMPILING `CombatExtended.Building_TurretGunCE`.** It derives from `Building_Turret`, NOT `Building_TurretGun`, so `Patch_BuildingTurretGun_ABBandLocalForcedTarget` never runs on it. And `CanSetForcedTarget => mannableComp != null && PlayerControlled` - **in CE, force-targeting exists ONLY on MANNABLE turrets**, so the forced-target path IS the manned-gun path. Its `OrderAttack` does the raw `(targ.Cell - Position).LengthHorizontal` against `minRange` and `range`: §1's slicing rule, wrong in both directions across bands.

**88.2 THE PLAN.**
- **PART 1 (essential): `Building_TurretGunCE.OrderAttack`.** House pattern: a reflection-only, `Prepare()`-shape-validated prefix handling ONLY the cross-band case - re-run the two limits band-locally via `ABCombatV2.TrySolve`, then replicate CE's short tail (`forcedTarget = targ`, `TryStartShootSomething(false)`, the holdFire message). Same-band orders fall through untouched. ⚠ Rejected: a transpiler (fragile blind), and translating `targ` for the duration (CE sets `currentTargetInt` inside the body, so the gun would fire at the translated cell for a tick).
- **PART 2: `CompFireArc.WithinFireArc`** - both `OrderAttack` and `IsValidTarget` gate on it and the angle is raw geometry. Only defs carrying the comp.
- **PART 3: acquisition - VERIFY, DON'T ASSUME (rule 54).** `TargSearcher()` returns the MANNING PAWN when manned; a non-`NonSnap` gun then goes through vanilla `AttackTargetFinder.BestShootTargetFromCurrentPosition`, which our §42 postfix covers. Believed fine, unproven. ⚠ A def carrying `NonSnapTurretExtension` uses CE's own `NonSnapAttackTargetFinder` and is NOT covered.
- **PART 4: `DrawRangeRings`** - `GenDraw.DrawRadiusRing(Position, range)`, i.e. §83.7's "turret ring from another band" gap, now with an owner.

**⚠ 88.3 TESTING IS THE EXPENSIVE PART.** Needs `isolated:false` or a `companionMods` launch with CE and its dependency chain - heavier and noisier than any window-12/13 test.

# 89. THE STACKED-PAWN STALL — **DIAGNOSED IN #395, NOT FIXED**

Five sightings across four runs (Rogue x2, Rynyk, Hunin, now Jay). Signature is always identical: `moving=True`, `path=FOUND`, `CanReach=True`, destination stable, **not advancing**. First four were `GotoWander`; #395's was a player-ordered `Goto`, which rules out anything wander-specific. Visible only since §85.16 turned `ABStuckWatchdog` on by default.

**⚠⚠ 89a THE TELL, AND OUR PROBE WAS BLIND TO IT (rule 71).** #395 logged `Jay at (63,0,458) ... nextCell=(63,0,458) walkable=True occupant=none`. **The pather's next cell is the cell the pawn is already standing on**, which is why nothing downstream looks wrong and why the watchdog's own verdict (`BLOCKED - movement is obstructed`) is a misattribution: nothing is obstructing it, it is stepping onto itself.

**THE VANILLA MECHANISM, and it is an infinite early return.** `Pawn_PathFollower.PatherTick` opens with `if (WillCollideWithPawnAt(pawn.Position, forceOnlyStanding: true, useId: true))` - i.e. *another standing pawn is on MY cell*. It then tries `CellFinder.TryFindBestPawnStandCell`; on failure it stamps `failedToFindCloseUnoccupiedCellTicks`, and every subsequent tick `FailedToFindCloseUnoccupiedCellRecently()` returns true and **`PatherTick` returns before any movement code**. `moving` stays true, the path stays found, `nextCell` never leaves `Position`. Exactly the observed state.

**⚠ WHY THE PROBE SAID `occupant=none`:** `ABStuckWatchdog` does `next.GetFirstPawn(map)` and then `occupant != p`. For a self-stack, `GetFirstPawn` returns Jay, the `!= p` test rejects him, and it prints `none`. **The one arrangement that matters is the one the probe cannot express.** FIX FIRST, BEFORE THEORISING FURTHER: count every pawn on the cell and print them all.

**⚠ IS IT OURS? UNPROVEN, AND THERE IS A PLAUSIBLE PATH.** §78's hold parks a crossing pawn on the mouth cell with `StopDead()` for 90 ticks, and §85.19 queues others onto the approach tile - both are deliberate ways to get two pawns near one cell. But `pendingTransit=False` on #395's pawn and band 1 on the earlier four, and pawns legitimately stack in vanilla (drafted moves, doorways). Rule 18: do not exonerate on one sample and do not convict on a hypothesis. The counted-occupant log line settles it in one run.
